questions.text: In a certain code language, 'PENCIL' is written as 'QFODJM'. How will 'PAPER' be written in that code?
questions.solution: Shortcut: Compare the first letters P→Q (+1) and last letters L→M (+1) to confirm a uniform +1 shift. Apply +1 to each letter of PAPER: P→Q, A→B, P→Q, E→F, R→S → QBQFS. Step-by-step: The pattern is each letter replaced by its immediate next letter in the alphabet (Position +1). P(16)→Q(17), E(5)→F(6), N(14)→O(15), C(3)→D(4), I(9)→J(10), L(12)→M(13). Applying same logic to PAPER gives QBQFS.

questions.text: Rohan walks 15 metres towards East. He then turns left and walks 20 metres. He turns left again and walks 15 metres. Finally, he turns right and walks 10 metres. How far is he from the starting point and in which direction?
questions.solution: Shortcut: Track Net Displacement. East-West: +15 (East) then -15 (West) = 0. North-South: +20 (North) then +10 (North) = 30m North. Distance = 30m North. Step-by-step: Start at Origin. 1. East 15m → (15, 0). 2. Left (North) 20m → (15, 20). 3. Left (West) 15m → (0, 20). 4. Right (North) 10m → (0, 30). Final position is 30m North of start.

questions.text: Select the letter that will come next in the following series: A, C, F, J, O, ?
questions.solution: Shortcut: Convert letters to their positional values (A=1, C=3, F=6, J=10, O=15). Find the differences: +2, +3, +4, +5. The difference increases by 1 each step. Next difference is +6. 15 + 6 = 21. The 21st letter is U. Step-by-step: Position of A=1. C=3 (diff +2). F=6 (diff +3). J=10 (diff +4). O=15 (diff +5). Pattern of differences is consecutive integers starting from 2. Next difference = 6. Required position = 15 + 6 = 21. 21st letter of alphabet = U.

questions.text: Who was the first recipient of the Param Vir Chakra, India's highest wartime gallantry award?
questions.solution: Shortcut: Eliminate options associated with the 1999 Kargil War (Batra, Pandey) and 1987 Siachen (Bana Singh). The PVC was instituted in 1950; the first action was the 1947-48 Kashmir operations. Worked Solution: Major Somnath Sharma of 4 Kumaon was awarded the first PVC posthumously for his actions on 3 November 1947 at Badgam, Kashmir. Captain Vikram Batra and Lt Manoj Pandey received PVCs for Kargil (1999). Subedar Major Bana Singh received PVC for Operation Rajiv (Siachen, 1987).

questions.text: What is the minimum age required to become the Prime Minister of India?
questions.solution: Shortcut: Link PM eligibility to Lok Sabha membership (Article 84). The PM must be a member of Parliament; the lower house (Lok Sabha) minimum age is 25 years. Rajya Sabha is 30 years. Since PM can be from Lok Sabha, the effective minimum is 25. Worked Solution: As per Article 84 of the Constitution, a person must be a citizen of India and not less than 25 years of age to be a member of the Lok Sabha. Since the Prime Minister must be a member of either House of Parliament (or get elected within 6 months), the minimum constitutional age is 25 years. Age for President/Vice President/Governor is 35 years; Rajya Sabha/State Legislative Council is 30 years.

questions.text: The 'Mangalyaan' mission (Mars Orbiter Mission) was launched by ISRO in which year?
questions.solution: Shortcut: Remember the 'Diwali Launch' trick. MOM was launched on 5 November 2013 (Diwali week) via PSLV-C25. It entered Mars orbit on 24 September 2014. Worked Solution: The Mars Orbiter Mission (MOM), colloquially Mangalyaan, was launched on 5 November 2013 from Satish Dhawan Space Centre, Sriharikota. It made India the first Asian nation to reach Martian orbit and the first nation in the world to do so in its maiden attempt. The launch year 2013 is the key fact.

questions.text: Who was the last Mughal Emperor of India?
questions.solution: Shortcut: Eliminate Aurangzeb (died 1707, peak of empire). Eliminate Shah Alam II (reigned 1759-1806, Battle of Buxar). The name 'Zafar' is synonymous with the 1857 Revolt and exile to Rangoon. Worked Solution: Bahadur Shah Zafar (Abu Zafar Siraj-ud-din Muhammad Bahadur Shah Zafar) was the 20th and last Mughal Emperor. He reigned from 1837 to 1857. After the Indian Rebellion of 1857, the British exiled him to Rangoon (Yangon), Burma, where he died in 1862, marking the formal end of the Mughal dynasty.

questions.text: How many Fundamental Duties are currently specified in the Constitution of India under Article 51A?
questions.solution: Shortcut (Option Elimination): Remember the amendment timeline. The 42nd Amendment (1976) added 10 duties. The 86th Amendment (2002) added 1 more duty regarding elementary education. Eliminate 10 (old count), 9, and 12. The correct total is 11. Full Solution: Fundamental Duties were incorporated in Part IV-A (Article 51A) by the 42nd Constitutional Amendment Act, 1976 on the recommendation of the Swaran Singh Committee, initially numbering 10. Subsequently, the 86th Constitutional Amendment Act, 2002 added the 11th duty: "Who is a parent or guardian to provide opportunities for education to his child or, as the case may be, ward between the age of six and fourteen years." Thus, the current total is 11.

questions.text: Find the unit digit of the product (7^95 × 3^58).
questions.solution: Shortcut: Use cyclicity of unit digits. For 7, cycle (7,9,3,1) length 4; 95 mod 4 = 3 → unit digit 3. For 3, cycle (3,9,7,1) length 4; 58 mod 4 = 2 → unit digit 9. Product unit digit = 3 × 9 = 27 → 7. Full: 7^95 = 7^(4×23+3) ends in 3. 3^58 = 3^(4×14+2) ends in 9. 3 × 9 = 27, so final unit digit is 7.

questions.text: A train 150 metres long crosses an electric pole in 15 seconds. How much time will it take to cross a platform 350 metres long?
questions.solution: Shortcut: Speed = Train Length / Time = 150/15 = 10 m/s. Total distance to cross platform = Train + Platform = 150 + 350 = 500 m. Time = Distance / Speed = 500/10 = 50 s. Full: Speed of train = 150 m / 15 s = 10 m/s. Distance to cover platform = 150 m + 350 m = 500 m. Required time = 500 m / 10 m/s = 50 seconds.

questions.text: The radii of two solid spheres are in the ratio 2 : 3. What is the ratio of their volumes?
questions.solution: Shortcut: For similar 3D shapes, volume ratio is the cube of the linear ratio. (2/3)^3 = 8/27. Full: Volume of sphere = (4/3)πr³. Ratio V1/V2 = (r1/r2)³ = (2/3)³ = 8/27.

questions.text: If x = √3 + √2, find the value of x² + 1/x².
questions.solution: Shortcut: Rationalize 1/x = 1/(√3+√2) = √3-√2. Then x + 1/x = (√3+√2) + (√3-√2) = 2√3. Use identity x² + 1/x² = (x + 1/x)² - 2 = (2√3)² - 2 = 12 - 2 = 10. Full: x = √3+√2. 1/x = √3-√2 (rationalizing). x + 1/x = 2√3. Squaring both sides: x² + 1/x² + 2 = 12. Therefore, x² + 1/x² = 10.

questions.text: A 5 kg object is lifted vertically through a height of 10 m. Taking g = 10 m/s², what is the work done against gravity?
questions.solution: Shortcut: Work against gravity = weight × height = (mg) × h. With g = 10 m/s², weight = 5 × 10 = 50 N. Multiply by 10 m gives 500 J. Full solution: Work done = force × displacement in direction of force. Force = mg = 5 kg × 10 m/s² = 50 N. Displacement = 10 m. Work = 50 N × 10 m = 500 J.

questions.text: Which of the following compounds contains nitrogen in the +5 oxidation state?
questions.solution: Shortcut: In a neutral compound, sum of oxidation states = 0. Oxygen is -2 each. For N2O5, total O = 5 × (-2) = -10. Let oxidation state of N be x. Then 2x + (-10) = 0 → 2x = +10 → x = +5. Full solution: Assign oxidation numbers: O = -2. For each option calculate N's oxidation state. NO: x -2 = 0 → x = +2. N2O5: 2x -10 = 0 → x = +5. NO2: x -4 = 0 → x = +4. N2O: 2x -2 = 0 → x = +1. Only N2O5 gives +5.

questions.text: Which organelle is known as the 'powerhouse of the cell'?
questions.solution: Shortcut: The term 'powerhouse' directly refers to mitochondria because it generates ATP through cellular respiration. Full solution: Mitochondria are double-membraned organelles where aerobic respiration occurs, producing ATP, the energy currency of the cell. Ribosomes synthesize proteins, the nucleus stores genetic material, and chloroplasts perform photosynthesis in plant cells. Hence, mitochondria is the correct answer.

questions.text: In a certain code language, 'PENCIL' is written as 'KVMXRO'. How will 'SHARP' be written in that language?
questions.solution: Shortcut: Recognize the Atbash cipher (Reverse Alphabet) where each letter is replaced by its mirror position (A↔Z, B↔Y). Sum of positions = 27. For 'SHARP': S(19)→H(8), H(8)→S(19), A(1)→Z(26), R(18)→I(9), P(16)→K(11). Full Solution: PENCIL→KVMXRO confirms P(16)→K(11), E(5)→V(22), N(14)→M(13), etc., each pair summing to 27. Applying 27−Position to SHARP gives H, S, Z, I, K → HSZIK.

questions.text: Rahul walks 10 km North, then turns right and walks 6 km. Then he turns right again and walks 10 km. Finally, he turns left and walks 5 km. How far is he from the starting point?
questions.solution: Shortcut: Net Displacement Method. Cancel opposite vertical movements (North 10 − South 10 = 0). Add horizontal movements in same direction (East 6 + East 5 = 11). Distance = 11 km. Full Solution: Start (0,0). North 10 → (0,10). Right (East) 6 → (6,10). Right (South) 10 → (6,0). Left (East) 5 → (11,0). Distance from origin = √(11²+0²) = 11 km.

questions.text: Pointing to a woman in a photograph, a man says, 'She is the only daughter of the father of my mother's brother.' How is the woman related to the man?
questions.solution: Shortcut (Back-tracking Method): Start from the man. Mother's brother = Maternal Uncle (+1 generation). Father of Uncle = Maternal Grandfather (+2 generations). Only daughter of Grandfather = Mother (since the man's mother is the only daughter). Step-by-step: 1. Man's Mother's Brother = Maternal Uncle. 2. Father of Maternal Uncle = Maternal Grandfather. 3. Only daughter of Maternal Grandfather = Man's Mother (as she has no sisters). Hence, the woman is the man's Mother.

questions.text: Which Article of the Indian Constitution is described as the 'Heart and Soul of the Constitution' by Dr. B.R. Ambedkar?
questions.solution: Shortcut: Associate 'Remedy' with 'Heart/Soul' — Article 32 provides the Right to Constitutional Remedies (writs), making other rights enforceable. Step-by-step: Dr. B.R. Ambedkar explicitly stated Article 32 is the most important article; it empowers citizens to move the Supreme Court directly for enforcement of Fundamental Rights via writs (Habeas Corpus, Mandamus, etc.). Article 19 covers Freedoms, Article 21 covers Life & Liberty, Article 14 covers Equality.

questions.text: Which is the largest state in India by geographical area?
questions.solution: Shortcut: Eliminate population leaders (UP, Maharashtra) — area leaders are usually central/western large states (Rajasthan, MP). Rajasthan (~3.42 lakh sq km) > MP (~3.08 lakh sq km). Step-by-step: As per Census 2011, Rajasthan covers 342,239 sq km, making it the largest. Madhya Pradesh is second. Maharashtra is third. Uttar Pradesh is fourth in area but first in population.

questions.text: Who was the first Governor-General of India (after the Charter Act of 1833)?
questions.solution: Shortcut: Distinguish 'Bengal' vs 'India' — Warren Hastings was first GG of *Bengal* (1773); Charter Act 1833 redesignated the post to GG of *India* — first holder was William Bentinck. Step-by-step: The Regulating Act 1773 created Governor-General of Bengal (Warren Hastings). The Charter Act 1833 changed the title to Governor-General of India. Lord William Bentinck (1833–1835) became the first to hold this new title. Lord Cornwallis and Lord Dalhousie served later.

questions.text: Which is the highest peacetime gallantry award in India?
questions.solution: Shortcut: 'Peace' = Ashoka (Emperor of Peace/Dharma Chakra) — Param Vir Chakra is *wartime* highest. Ashoka Chakra is peacetime equivalent. Step-by-step: Gallantry awards are categorized into Wartime (Param Vir Chakra, Maha Vir Chakra, Vir Chakra) and Peacetime (Ashoka Chakra, Kirti Chakra, Shaurya Chakra). Ashoka Chakra is the highest peacetime decoration for valour, courageous action or self-sacrifice away from the battlefield. Param Vir Chakra is the highest wartime award.

questions.text: Who is the ex-officio Chairman of the Rajya Sabha?
questions.solution: Shortcut: Use Option Elimination based on Constitutional designations. The President is Head of State (not RS Chair), the PM is Head of Government (usually LS member), and the Speaker presides over Lok Sabha. Only the Vice President holds the ex-officio Chairmanship of Rajya Sabha. Step-by-step: Article 89(1) of the Indian Constitution explicitly states that the Vice President of India shall be the ex-officio Chairman of the Council of States (Rajya Sabha). The President summons Parliament but does not chair either house. The Prime Minister leads the Lower House typically. The Speaker is the presiding officer of Lok Sabha only.

questions.text: As per the table, the number of books sold by a bookstore in four successive months is shown. Which month had the highest percentage increase in sales compared to its previous month? Table: Month | Books Sold Jan | 120 Feb | 150 Mar | 180 Apr | 210
questions.solution: Shortcut: Percentage increase = (new‑old)/old ×100. Compare ratios: Feb/Jan =150/120=1.25 →25%; Mar/Feb=180/150=1.20 →20%; Apr/Mar=210/180=1.166… →16.7%. The largest is 25% for February. Full: Compute each increase as above; February gives the maximum percentage rise, so option A is correct.

questions.text: Find the unit digit of the expression (7^95 + 3^58).
questions.solution: Shortcut: Use cyclicity of unit digits (cycle of 4). For 7^95: 95 mod 4 = 3, 3rd position in cycle (7,9,3,1) is 3. For 3^58: 58 mod 4 = 2, 2nd position in cycle (3,9,7,1) is 9. Sum of unit digits = 3 + 9 = 12, unit digit is 2. Full: 7^95 = 7^(4*23+3) → unit digit of 7^3=343 is 3. 3^58 = 3^(4*14+2) → unit digit of 3^2=9 is 9. 3+9=12 → unit digit 2.

questions.text: A copper wire is bent in the form of a circle of radius 14 cm. If the same wire is bent into a square, what is the area of the square? (Use π = 22/7)
questions.solution: Shortcut: Perimeter remains constant. Circumference = 2 × (22/7) × 14 = 88 cm. Side of square = 88/4 = 22 cm. Area = 22² = 484 cm². Full: Length of wire = 2πr = 2 × (22/7) × 14 = 88 cm. This length becomes perimeter of square: 4a = 88 → a = 22 cm. Area = a² = 22 × 22 = 484 cm².

questions.text: The angle of elevation of the top of a tower from a point on the ground 30 m away from the foot of the tower is 30°. Find the height of the tower.
questions.solution: Shortcut: Use standard ratio for 30°-60°-90° triangle (1 : √3 : 2). tan 30° = 1/√3 = Height / 30 → Height = 30/√3 = 10√3 m. Full: In right triangle, tan(30°) = Perpendicular / Base = Height / 30. 1/√3 = h/30 → h = 30/√3. Rationalizing denominator: h = (30√3)/3 = 10√3 m.

questions.text: A straight wire of length 0.5 m carries a current of 2 A in a uniform magnetic field of 0.4 T. If the wire is oriented perpendicular to the field direction, what is the magnitude of the magnetic force acting on the wire?
questions.solution: Shortcut: Use F = BIL sinθ. Since θ = 90°, sinθ = 1. Multiply B × I × L = 0.4 × 2 × 0.5. Notice 2 × 0.5 = 1, so Force = 0.4 × 1 = 0.4 N instantly. Full Solution: Magnetic force on a current-carrying conductor is given by F = B I L sinθ. Substituting B = 0.4 T, I = 2 A, L = 0.5 m, θ = 90°: F = 0.4 × 2 × 0.5 × 1 = 0.4 N.

questions.text: An iron nail is dipped in a solution of copper sulphate (CuSO₄) for some time. Which of the following observations is correct based on the reactivity series?

options.label: A
options.text: The blue colour of the solution intensifies

options.label: B
options.text: No change occurs in the solution

options.label: C
options.text: The blue colour fades and a reddish-brown deposit forms on the nail

options.label: D
options.text: The solution turns green and the nail dissolves completely

questions.solution: Shortcut: Recall reactivity series mnemonic '... Fe ... (H) ... Cu ...'. Iron (Fe) is above Copper (Cu), so Fe displaces Cu²⁺. Reaction: Fe + CuSO₄ → FeSO₄ + Cu. Blue Cu²⁺ fades (replaced by pale green Fe²⁺), reddish-brown Cu metal deposits on nail. Eliminate options showing no change or intensifying blue. Full Solution: Iron is more reactive than copper. It displaces copper from its salt solution forming ferrous sulphate (light green) and copper metal (reddish-brown). The blue colour of CuSO₄ fades as Cu²⁺ ions are reduced to Cu(s), which coats the nail.

questions.text: Which hormone, secreted by the beta cells of the Islets of Langerhans in the pancreas, lowers the blood glucose level by promoting its uptake into cells?
questions.solution: Shortcut: Mnemonic — 'Insulin puts sugar **In** cells'. Glucagon, Adrenaline, and Cortisol all **increase** blood glucose (hyperglycemic). Only Insulin decreases it (hypoglycemic). Eliminate the three 'stress/raise' hormones. Full Solution: Insulin is a peptide hormone secreted by β-cells of pancreatic Islets of Langerhans. It binds to tyrosine kinase receptors triggering GLUT4 translocation, facilitating glucose uptake in muscle/adipose tissue, lowering blood glucose. Glucagon (α-cells), Adrenaline (adrenal medulla), and Cortisol (adrenal cortex) act via cAMP to increase hepatic glucose output.

questions.text: Find the missing term in the following alphabet series: A, C, F, J, O, ?
questions.solution: Shortcut: Write alphabet positions (A=1, B=2... using EJOTY for 5,10,15,20,25). Differences between terms: +2, +3, +4, +5. Next difference is +6. O(15) + 6 = 21 (U). Worked Solution: A(1) -> C(3) diff 2; C(3) -> F(6) diff 3; F(6) -> J(10) diff 4; J(10) -> O(15) diff 5. Pattern increases by 1 each step. Next diff = 6. 15 + 6 = 21 -> U.

questions.text: In a certain code language, vowels are coded as the next letter and consonants are coded as the previous letter in the English alphabet. How will 'ORANGE' be written in that code?
questions.solution: Shortcut: Identify vowels (A,E,I,O,U) -> Next letter (+1). Consonants -> Previous letter (-1). Apply quickly without writing full alphabet. Worked Solution: O(vowel)->P; R(cons)->Q; A(vowel)->B; N(cons)->M; G(cons)->F; E(vowel)->F. Result: PQBMFF.

questions.text: Pointing to a man in a photograph, a woman said, 'He is the son of the only son of my grandfather.' How is the man related to the woman?
questions.solution: Shortcut: Draw family tree. 'Only son of my grandfather' = Woman's Father. 'Son of (Father)' = Woman's Brother (or herself, but 'He' implies male sibling). Worked Solution: Woman's Grandfather's only son is Woman's Father. The man is the son of Woman's Father. Therefore, the man is Woman's Brother.

questions.text: The 'Instrument of Accession' signed by Maharaja Hari Singh in October 1947 legally acceded which princely state to the Dominion of India?
questions.solution: Shortcut (Elimination Technique): Hyderabad (Option A) was integrated via Operation Polo in 1948. Junagadh (Option B) acceded to Pakistan initially, then India after a plebiscite. Travancore (Option D) initially declared independence but joined India before 1947 end. Only Jammu & Kashmir (Option C) executed the Instrument of Accession on 26 Oct 1947 under specific circumstances. Step-by-step: The Instrument of Accession was a legal document executed by Maharaja Hari Singh on 26 October 1947. By executing this document under the provisions of the Indian Independence Act 1947, the Maharaja agreed to accede the princely state of Jammu and Kashmir to the Dominion of India. Lord Mountbatten accepted it on 27 October 1947.
questions.topic: Modern Indian History (Integration of Princely States)

questions.text: Which of the following rivers does NOT originate from the Amarkantak plateau?
questions.solution: Shortcut (Elimination Technique): Amarkantak (Maikal Hills) is a major watershed. Narmada (A) flows West; Son (B) flows North; Mahanadi (C) flows East. All three originate here. Tapti (D) originates from Multai in Betul district (Satpura range), South of Amarkantak. Eliminate A, B, C as they share the source. Step-by-step: The Amarkantak plateau in Anuppur district, Madhya Pradesh, is the source of three major rivers: Narmada (westward), Son (northward, tributary of Ganga), and Mahanadi (eastward). The Tapti river originates from the Satpura range near Multai in Betul district, Madhya Pradesh, which is geographically distinct from the Amarkantak plateau.

questions.text: Under which Article of the Constitution of India is the 'Annual Financial Statement' (Union Budget) laid before Parliament?
questions.solution: Shortcut (Elimination Technique): Article 110 defines 'Money Bill'. Article 112 mandates the 'Annual Financial Statement'. Article 114 deals with 'Appropriation Bills'. Article 116 covers 'Votes on Account, Votes of Credit and Exceptional Grants'. The keyword 'Statement' maps directly to Article 112. Step-by-step: Article 112 of the Constitution of India stipulates that the President shall in respect of every financial year cause to be laid before both Houses of Parliament a statement of the estimated expenditure and receipts of the Government of India. This statement is constitutionally termed the 'Annual Financial Statement' and is popularly known as the Union Budget.

questions.text: Which vitamin deficiency causes 'Night Blindness' (Nyctalopia)?
questions.solution: Shortcut (Elimination Technique): Vitamin B12 deficiency causes Pernicious Anemia/Neurological issues. Vitamin C deficiency causes Scurvy. Vitamin D deficiency causes Rickets/Osteomalacia. Vitamin A is the only one directly linked to Rhodopsin (visual pigment) synthesis and retinal health. Step-by-step: Vitamin A (Retinol) is a critical component of Rhodopsin, the photopigment in rod cells of the retina responsible for vision in low-light conditions. A deficiency impairs the regeneration of rhodopsin, leading to Nyctalopia (Night Blindness). It is also the leading cause of preventable childhood blindness (Xerophthalmia).

questions.text: Exercise 'Dharma Guardian' is a joint military exercise conducted between the Indian Army and the army of which country?
questions.solution: Shortcut (Elimination Technique): 'Shakti' is with France (B). 'AustraHind' is with Australia (C). 'Ajeya Warrior' is with UK (D). 'Dharma Guardian' is the specific annual exercise with Japan (A) focusing on counter-terrorism and disaster relief. Step-by-step: Exercise Dharma Guardian is a bilateral joint military exercise between the Indian Army and the Japan Ground Self-Defense Force (JGSDF). It commenced in 2018 and is held annually in alternating locations (India and Japan). It focuses on sharing best practices in counter-terrorism operations, jungle warfare, and Humanitarian Assistance and Disaster Relief (HADR) under UN mandate.

questions.text: The HCF and LCM of two numbers are 12 and 720 respectively. If one of the numbers is 60, what is the other number?
questions.solution: Shortcut: Use the fundamental relation Product of two numbers = HCF × LCM. The second number = (HCF × LCM) / First Number = (12 × 720) / 60. Cancel 60 with 720 to get 12, then 12 × 12 = 144. Step-by-step: Let the other number be x. We know HCF = 12, LCM = 720, and one number = 60. Formula: 60 × x = 12 × 720. Solving for x: x = (12 × 720) / 60 = 12 × 12 = 144.

questions.text: A solid metallic sphere of radius 6 cm is melted and recast into a solid right circular cylinder of radius 4 cm. The height of the cylinder is:
questions.solution: Shortcut: Volume remains constant during melting. Equate Volume of Sphere = Volume of Cylinder. (4/3)πr³ = πR²h. Cancel π. h = (4/3 × 6³) / 4² = (4/3 × 216) / 16 = 288 / 16 = 18 cm. Step-by-step: Volume of sphere = (4/3)π(6)³ = (4/3)π(216) = 288π cm³. Volume of cylinder = π(4)²h = 16πh cm³. Equating: 16πh = 288π => h = 288/16 = 18 cm.

questions.text: The value of tan 10° × tan 20° × tan 30° × tan 40° × tan 50° × tan 60° × tan 70° × tan 80° is:
questions.solution: Shortcut: Use complementary angle identity tan(90°−θ) = cot θ. Pair terms: (tan 10° × tan 80°) = tan 10° × cot 10° = 1. Similarly (20°,70°), (30°,60°), (40°,50°) each multiply to 1. Product = 1 × 1 × 1 × 1 = 1. Step-by-step: tan 80° = cot 10°, tan 70° = cot 20°, tan 60° = cot 30°, tan 50° = cot 40°. Expression becomes (tan 10° cot 10°) × (tan 20° cot 20°) × (tan 30° cot 30°) × (tan 40° cot 40°) = 1 × 1 × 1 × 1 = 1.

questions.text: What is the unit digit of (7^95 − 3^58)?
questions.solution: Shortcut: Use cyclicity of 4 for unit digits. For 7^95: 95 ÷ 4 remainder 3 → unit digit of 7³ = 3. For 3^58: 58 ÷ 4 remainder 2 → unit digit of 3² = 9. Subtract: 3 − 9 = −6 → borrow 10 → unit digit 4. Step-by-step: Cyclicity of 7 is 7,9,3,1. 95 mod 4 = 3 → 3rd position = 3. Cyclicity of 3 is 3,9,7,1. 58 mod 4 = 2 → 2nd position = 9. Unit digit of difference = (10 + 3) − 9 = 4.

questions.text: A body starts from rest and moves with a uniform acceleration of 4 m/s². The distance travelled by the body in the 5th second of its motion is:
questions.solution: Shortcut: For a body starting from rest (u=0), distance travelled in the nth second = a × (n - 0.5). Here, a = 4 m/s² and n = 5. Distance = 4 × (5 - 0.5) = 4 × 4.5 = 18 m. Full Solution: Using the formula for displacement in the nth second: S_n = u + (a/2)(2n - 1). Given u = 0, a = 4 m/s², n = 5. S_5 = 0 + (4/2)(2×5 - 1) = 2 × 9 = 18 m.

questions.text: The oxide of an element 'X' has the formula X₂O₃. What will be the formula of its chloride?
questions.solution: Shortcut: Use the cross-valency rule. In X₂O₃, oxygen has valency 2. Cross-multiplying gives valency of X = 3. Since chlorine has valency 1, the formula of chloride is XCl₃. Full Solution: In X₂O₃, let oxidation state of X be x. Oxygen is -2. 2x + 3(-2) = 0 → 2x = 6 → x = +3. Valency of X is 3. Chlorine (Cl) has valency 1. To balance valencies, one atom of X combines with three atoms of Cl. Formula = XCl₃.

questions.text: The filtration of blood in the human nephron takes place specifically in which capillary network under high pressure?
questions.solution: Shortcut: Remember the functional sequence: Filtration → Glomerulus (high pressure capillary bed); Selective Reabsorption → PCT; Concentration of Urine → Loop of Henle. Filtration occurs only in the Glomerulus. Full Solution: The glomerulus is a tuft of capillaries formed by the afferent arteriole (wider) and efferent arteriole (narrower). This difference in diameter creates high hydrostatic pressure inside the glomerular capillaries, forcing water and solutes out of the blood into the Bowman's capsule (ultrafiltration). The PCT and Loop of Henle are tubular structures involved in reabsorption, not the primary site of filtration.

questions.text: Select the number that will come next in the following series: 2, 6, 12, 20, 30, ?
questions.solution: Shortcut: Check differences between terms: 4, 6, 8, 10. Differences increase by 2 each time. Next difference = 12. 30 + 12 = 42. Full Method: The series follows the pattern n × (n+1): 1×2=2, 2×3=6, 3×4=12, 4×5=20, 5×6=30. The 6th term is 6×7 = 42. Alternatively, successive differences are consecutive even numbers (4, 6, 8, 10), so next difference is 12, giving 30+12=42.

questions.text: Introducing a boy, a girl said, 'He is the son of the only daughter of the father of my brother.' How is the boy related to the girl?
questions.solution: Shortcut: Decode backwards from the last relation. 'Father of my brother' = My Father. 'Only daughter of my Father' = Me (the speaker/girl). 'Son of me' = My Son. Worked Solution: The phrase 'father of my brother' refers to the girl's father. The 'only daughter' of that father is the girl herself (as she has no sisters implied by 'only daughter'). The boy is the 'son' of that daughter, making him the girl's son.

questions.text: In a certain code language, 'GIVE' is written as '79225' and 'BOAT' is written as '215120'. How will 'MOON' be written in that language?
questions.solution: Shortcut: Use the EJOTY concept (E=5, J=10, O=15, T=20, Y=25) to instantly recall alphabet positions. The code is the concatenation of positional values. M=13, O=15, O=15, N=14 → 13151514. Full Solution: Decode the logic from examples. G(7) I(9) V(22) E(5) → 79225. B(2) O(15) A(1) T(20) → 215120. Each letter is replaced by its position in the English alphabet. Applying same to MOON: M(13), O(15), O(15), N(14) = 13151514.

questions.text: Arrange the following major events of the Indian Freedom Struggle in correct chronological order (Earliest to Latest): 1. Jallianwala Bagh Massacre 2. Non-Cooperation Movement 3. Quit India Movement 4. Partition of Bengal
questions.solution: Shortcut: Use anchor years for rapid elimination. Partition of Bengal (1905) is the earliest. Jallianwala Bagh (1919) precedes Non-Cooperation (1920-22). Quit India (1942) is the latest. Only Option A follows the sequence 1905 -> 1919 -> 1920 -> 1942. Worked Solution: Partition of Bengal by Lord Curzon occurred in 1905. Jallianwala Bagh Massacre took place on April 13, 1919. Non-Cooperation Movement was launched by Gandhi in September 1920. Quit India Movement started in August 1942. The correct chronological order is 4, 1, 2, 3.

questions.text: Which of the following mountain peaks is the highest peak located entirely within Indian territory?
questions.solution: Shortcut: Eliminate border peaks first. K2 lies in Pakistan-occupied Kashmir (POK). Kanchenjunga is shared with Nepal. Nanda Devi (7,816 m) lies entirely in Uttarakhand, India. Kamet (7,756 m) is also in India but lower than Nanda Devi. Worked Solution: K2 (8,611 m) is the world's second-highest peak but is located in the Gilgit-Baltistan region of POK. Kanchenjunga (8,586 m) is the third-highest globally but straddles the India-Nepal border. Nanda Devi (7,816 m) is the highest peak situated completely within India. Kamet is the second-highest peak entirely in India but is lower than Nanda Devi.

questions.text: As per the original text of the Constitution of India adopted on 26th November 1949, how many Schedules did it contain?
questions.solution: Shortcut: Remember the baseline 'Original 8, Current 12'. The 9th Schedule was added in 1951 (1st Amendment), 10th in 1985 (52nd Amendment), 11th & 12th in 1992 (73rd & 74th Amendments). Option A (Eight) is the only figure matching the 1949 status. Worked Solution: The Constitution of India, when adopted on 26 November 1949, had 395 Articles, 22 Parts, and 8 Schedules. The 9th Schedule was inserted by the 1st Constitutional Amendment Act, 1951. The 10th Schedule (Anti-Defection) was added by the 52nd Amendment Act, 1985. The 11th Schedule (Panchayats) and 12th Schedule (Municipalities) were added by the 73rd and 74th Amendment Acts, 1992 respectively, bringing the current total to 12.

questions.text: Deficiency of which vitamin is the primary cause of Night Blindness (Nyctalopia)?
questions.solution: Shortcut: Use Disease-Vitamin mapping elimination. Vitamin C deficiency causes Scurvy. Vitamin D deficiency causes Rickets/Osteomalacia. Vitamin B12 deficiency causes Pernicious Anemia. By eliminating the three known pairs, Vitamin A is the only option left for Night Blindness. Worked Solution: Vitamin A (Retinol) is a critical component of rhodopsin, the light-sensitive pigment in retinal rod cells essential for low-light vision. Its deficiency leads to xerophthalmia and night blindness. Vitamin B12 deficiency leads to megaloblastic anemia and neurological issues. Vitamin C deficiency causes scurvy (bleeding gums, poor wound healing). Vitamin D deficiency causes rickets in children and osteomalacia in adults.

questions.text: The 'Agni' series of missiles developed by DRDO under the Integrated Guided Missile Development Programme (IGMDP) are categorized as:
questions.solution: Shortcut: Use DRDO Missile Name-Class association. 'Akash' = Surface-to-Air. 'Nag' = Anti-Tank. 'Astra' = Air-to-Air. 'Prithvi' & 'Agni' = Surface-to-Surface Ballistic. Option C matches the Agni class. Worked Solution: The IGMDP developed five missile systems. Prithvi (Short-range) and Agni (Intermediate/Intercontinental-range) are Surface-to-Surface Ballistic Missiles. Akash is a Medium-range Surface-to-Air Missile. Nag is a Third-generation Anti-Tank Guided Missile. Trishul (short-range SAM) and Astra (Beyond Visual Range Air-to-Air) were later additions. Agni missiles are strategic nuclear-capable ballistic missiles launched from land (surface) to hit land targets (surface).

questions.text: If the radius of a sphere is increased by 20%, what is the percentage increase in its volume?
questions.solution: Shortcut: Volume ∝ r³. New radius factor = 1.2. Volume factor = (1.2)³ = 1.728. % Increase = (1.728 - 1) × 100 = 72.8%. Worked: Original Volume V₁ = (4/3)πr³. New radius = 1.2r. New Volume V₂ = (4/3)π(1.2r)³ = 1.728 × (4/3)πr³ = 1.728 V₁. Increase = 0.728 V₁ = 72.8%.

questions.text: A and B together can complete a work in 12 days. B and C together can complete it in 15 days. C and A together can complete it in 20 days. In how many days can A alone complete the work?
questions.solution: Shortcut: LCM Method. Total Work = LCM(12, 15, 20) = 60 units. Efficiency (A+B) = 5 units/day, (B+C) = 4 units/day, (C+A) = 3 units/day. Adding: 2(A+B+C) = 12 units/day => (A+B+C) = 6 units/day. Efficiency of A = 6 - 4 = 2 units/day. Time for A = 60/2 = 30 days. Full Method: 1/A + 1/B = 1/12, 1/B + 1/C = 1/15, 1/C + 1/A = 1/20. Adding gives 2(1/A+1/B+1/C) = 1/5 => 1/A+1/B+1/C = 1/10. Subtracting 1/B+1/C=1/15 gives 1/A = 1/10 - 1/15 = 1/30. Time = 30 days.

questions.text: The angle of elevation of the top of a tower from a point on the ground is 30°. On walking 20 metres towards the tower, the angle of elevation becomes 60°. What is the height of the tower (in metres)?
questions.solution: Shortcut: Formula for height when angles are 30° and 60°: h = d / (cot 30° - cot 60°) = 20 / (√3 - 1/√3) = 20 / (2/√3) = 10√3 m. Full Method: Let height = h. In Δ with 60°, base = h/√3. In Δ with 30°, base = h√3. Difference in bases = h√3 - h/√3 = 20. => h(3-1)/√3 = 20 => 2h/√3 = 20 => h = 10√3 m.

questions.text: What is the unit digit of the expression \((12^{41} + 13^{31} + 17^{21} + 18^{11})\)?
questions.solution: Shortcut: Use cyclicity of 4 for unit digits 2,3,7,8. Powers 41,31,21,11 give remainders 1,3,1,3 yielding unit digits 2,7,7,2; sum=18→8. Full: \(12^{41}\to2^{41}\to2^1=2\); \(13^{31}\to3^{31}\to3^3=7\); \(17^{21}\to7^{21}\to7^1=7\); \(18^{11}\to8^{11}\to8^3=2\); total unit digit \(=(2+7+7+2)=18\to8\).

questions.text: Three resistors of 2 Ω, 3 Ω, and 6 Ω are connected in parallel across a battery. What is the equivalent resistance of the combination?
questions.solution: Shortcut: For parallel resistors, calculate the sum of reciprocals: 1/2 + 1/3 + 1/6 = (3+2+1)/6 = 1. The equivalent resistance is the reciprocal of this sum, i.e., 1/1 = 1 Ω. Full Method: Using the formula 1/Req = 1/R1 + 1/R2 + 1/R3. Substituting values: 1/Req = 1/2 + 1/3 + 1/6 = 1. Therefore, Req = 1 Ω.

questions.text: What is the oxidation state of Chlorine (Cl) in Potassium Chlorate (KClO₃)?
questions.solution: Shortcut: The algebraic sum of oxidation states in a neutral compound is zero. K is +1 (Group 1), O is -2 (×3 = -6). Let Cl be x: +1 + x - 6 = 0 → x = +5. Full Method: Assign known oxidation states: Potassium (+1), Oxygen (-2 each). Set up equation: (+1) + x + 3(-2) = 0. Solving gives x - 5 = 0, so x = +5.

questions.text: What is the correct sequence of components in a reflex arc through which a nerve impulse travels during a reflex action?

options.label: A
options.text: Receptor → Interneuron → Sensory Neuron → Motor Neuron → Effector

options.label: B
options.text: Receptor → Sensory Neuron → Interneuron → Motor Neuron → Effector

options.label: C
options.text: Sensory Neuron → Receptor → Interneuron → Motor Neuron → Effector

options.label: D
options.text: Effector → Motor Neuron → Interneuron → Sensory Neuron → Receptor

questions.solution: Shortcut: Use the mnemonic 'RSIME' (Receptor, Sensory neuron, Interneuron, Motor neuron, Effector). The impulse flows from the receptor towards the CNS via sensory neuron, crosses synapse to interneuron, then to motor neuron, and finally to the effector. Full Method: A reflex arc starts at the Receptor (detects stimulus) → Sensory Neuron (carries to spinal cord) → Interneuron (relay in spinal cord) → Motor Neuron (carries to effector) → Effector (muscle/gland responds).

questions.text: In a certain code language, 'ROAD' is written as 'URDG'. How will 'SIGN' be written in that code language?
questions.solution: Shortcut: Compare the position values of the first letters (R=18, U=21) to detect a constant forward shift of +3. Apply +3 to each letter of 'SIGN'. Worked Solution: R+3=U, O+3=R, A+3=D, D+3=G confirms the pattern. For SIGN: S(19)+3=V(22), I(9)+3=L(12), G(7)+3=J(10), N(14)+3=Q(17). The coded word is VLJQ.

questions.text: Pointing to a photograph, a man said, "She is the only daughter of the only son of my father's father." How is the woman in the photograph related to the man?
questions.solution: Shortcut: 'Only son of my father's father' is my Father. 'Only daughter of my Father' is my Sister. Full Method: The man's father's father is his paternal grandfather. The only son of the grandfather is the man's father (assuming no paternal uncles). The only daughter of that father is the man's sister (or the man himself if female, but 'she' confirms female). Thus, the woman is the man's sister.

questions.text: Find the missing term in the following series: 2, 6, 12, 20, 30, ?
questions.solution: Shortcut: Recognize the pattern n × (n+1): 1×2=2, 2×3=6, 3×4=12, 4×5=20, 5×6=30. Next term is 6×7=42. Full Method: Calculate differences between consecutive terms: 4, 6, 8, 10. Differences increase by 2 each time. Next difference is 12. Add 12 to the last term 30 to get 42.

questions.text: Which river is known as the 'Sorrow of Bihar' due to its frequent flooding and shifting course?
questions.solution: Shortcut: Associate 'Sorrow' with high sediment load and flooding in North Bihar plains. Kosi is infamous for breaching embankments. Full Solution: The Kosi River carries a massive amount of silt from the Himalayas, causing its bed to rise and the river to frequently change course (avulsion). This leads to devastating floods in the plains of North Bihar almost every year, earning it the sobriquet 'Sorrow of Bihar'. The Damodar River was formerly called 'Sorrow of Bengal' (now controlled by DVC dams).

questions.text: Under which Article of the Indian Constitution is the 'Right to Constitutional Remedies' enshrined?
questions.solution: Shortcut: Dr. B.R. Ambedkar called Article 32 the 'Heart and Soul of the Constitution'. Remember '32' for 'Remedy/Teeth' to the Fundamental Rights. Full Solution: Article 32 provides the right to move the Supreme Court by appropriate proceedings for the enforcement of Fundamental Rights. It empowers the Supreme Court to issue directions, orders, or writs (Habeas Corpus, Mandamus, Prohibition, Quo Warranto, Certiorari). Article 226 grants similar power to High Courts. Article 14 is Equality before Law, Article 19 is Freedom of Speech etc., Article 21 is Protection of Life and Personal Liberty.

questions.text: Deficiency of which vitamin causes Rickets in children?
questions.solution: Shortcut: 'D' for 'D' (Rickets/D). Sunlight helps synthesize Vitamin D; lack of it softens bones (Rickets in kids, Osteomalacia in adults). Full Solution: Vitamin D (Calciferol) is essential for calcium and phosphorus absorption in the body. Its deficiency leads to defective mineralization of bones. In children, this manifests as Rickets (bow legs, pigeon chest, delayed dentition). Vitamin A deficiency causes Night Blindness/Xerophthalmia. Vitamin B1 (Thiamine) deficiency causes Beri-Beri. Vitamin C (Ascorbic Acid) deficiency causes Scurvy.

questions.text: How many Schedules are there in the Constitution of India?
questions.solution: Shortcut: Use elimination based on amendment history. The original Constitution had 8 Schedules. Four were added later: 9th (1951), 10th (1985), 11th (1992), 12th (1992). Total = 8 + 4 = 12. Full Solution: The Constitution of India originally contained 8 Schedules. Through various Constitutional Amendment Acts, four more Schedules were added: the 9th Schedule (Land Reforms), 10th Schedule (Anti-Defection Law), 11th Schedule (Powers of Panchayats), and 12th Schedule (Powers of Municipalities). No further Schedules have been added since 1992, making the current total 12.

questions.text: Which of the following Indian states has the largest geographical area?
questions.solution: Shortcut: Eliminate using relative size comparison. Rajasthan (342,239 km²) is clearly larger than Madhya Pradesh (308,252 km²) and Maharashtra (307,713 km²), which are close to each other but smaller. Uttar Pradesh (240,928 km²) is significantly smaller. Full Solution: Rajasthan is the largest state in India by area, covering approximately 342,239 square kilometers. It is followed by Madhya Pradesh (approx. 308,252 km²) and Maharashtra (approx. 307,713 km²), which are very close in size. Uttar Pradesh ranks fourth in area (approx. 240,928 km²) but is the most populous state.

questions.text: What is the unit digit of (7^2023 + 3^2024)?
questions.solution: Shortcut: Use cyclicity of unit digits. 7 has cycle 4 (7,9,3,1); 2023 mod 4 = 3 → unit digit 3. 3 has cycle 4 (3,9,7,1); 2024 mod 4 = 0 → unit digit 1. Sum = 3+1 = 4. Full: 7^1=7, 7^2=49→9, 7^3=343→3, 7^4=2401→1 repeats every 4. 2023 = 4×505+3 → unit digit of 7^2023 = 3. 3^1=3, 3^2=9, 3^3=27→7, 3^4=81→1 repeats every 4. 2024 = 4×506 → unit digit of 3^2024 = 1. 3+1=4.

questions.text: Find the smallest positive integer n such that the 10‑digit number 123456789n is divisible by 11.
questions.solution: Shortcut: Divisibility by 11 → difference between sum of digits in odd positions and even positions must be 0 or multiple of 11. For 123456789: odd positions (1,3,5,7,9) sum = 1+3+5+7+9 = 25; even positions (2,4,6,8) sum = 2+4+6+8 = 20. Difference = 5. Adding n at position 10 (even) makes even sum = 20+n. New difference = 25 − (20+n) = 5−n. For divisibility, 5−n = 0 ⇒ n = 5. Full: Check n=5 gives difference 0, so 1234567895 is divisible by 11.

questions.text: A shopkeeper marks his goods 40% above cost price and then allows a discount of 10%. What is his effective profit percent?
questions.solution: Shortcut: Successive percentage change formula: net% = a + b + ab/100, where a = +40% (markup), b = −10% (discount). Net = 40 − 10 + (40×−10)/100 = 30 − 4 = 26%. Full: Let CP = 100. MP = 140. SP after 10% discount = 140 × 0.9 = 126. Profit = 26 → Profit% = 26%.

questions.text: If a : b = 3 : 4 and b : c = 5 : 6, then a : c is equal to
questions.solution: Shortcut: Multiply the two ratios: a/c = (a/b) × (b/c) = (3/4) × (5/6) = 15/24 = 5/8 → a : c = 5 : 8. Full: Make b common. a:b = 3:4 = 15:20 (multiply by 5). b:c = 5:6 = 20:24 (multiply by 4). Hence a:b:c = 15:20:24 → a:c = 15:24 = 5:8.

questions.text: An object is placed at a distance of 30 cm from a convex lens of focal length 20 cm. What is the nature and position of the image formed?

options.label: A
options.text: Real, Inverted, 60 cm on the other side of the lens

options.label: B
options.text: Virtual, Erect, 60 cm on the same side of the lens

options.label: C
options.text: Real, Inverted, 12 cm on the other side of the lens

options.label: D
options.text: Virtual, Erect, 12 cm on the same side of the lens

questions.solution: Shortcut: Object distance (30 cm) lies between F (20 cm) and 2F (40 cm). For a convex lens, this always produces a Real, Inverted, Magnified image beyond 2F (v > 40 cm). Only option with v=60 cm fits. Step-by-step: Using lens formula 1/v - 1/u = 1/f with u = -30 cm, f = +20 cm. 1/v = 1/20 - 1/30 = 1/60 => v = +60 cm. Positive v confirms Real image on opposite side. Magnification m = v/u = -2 (Inverted, Magnified).

questions.text: What is the pH of a 0.001 M hydrochloric acid (HCl) solution? (Given log 10 = 1)
questions.solution: Shortcut: HCl is a strong monoprotic acid, so [H⁺] = Molarity = 1 × 10⁻³ M. pH = -log[H⁺] = -log(10⁻³) = 3. Step-by-step: Concentration = 0.001 M = 10⁻³ M. pH = -log₁₀(10⁻³) = - (log₁₀1 + log₁₀10⁻³) = - (0 - 3) = 3.

questions.text: In a grassland food chain (Grass → Grasshopper → Frog → Snake), the energy available at the producer level (Grass) is 10,000 J. Applying the 10% law of energy transfer, what is the energy available to the secondary consumer (Frog)?
questions.solution: Shortcut: Energy transfers twice (Producer → Primary → Secondary). Apply 10% twice: 10,000 × 0.1 × 0.1 = 100 J. Step-by-step: Energy at Producer = 10,000 J. Energy at Primary Consumer (Grasshopper) = 10% of 10,000 = 1,000 J. Energy at Secondary Consumer (Frog) = 10% of 1,000 = 100 J.

questions.text: In a certain code language, 'SOLDIER' is written as 'UQNFKGT'. How will 'AGNIVEER' be written in that same code language?
questions.solution: Shortcut: Check the shift using the first letter only: S → U is +2. Apply +2 to A → C. Only options A and B start with C. Check 2nd letter: G → I (+2). Both A and B have I. Check 3rd letter: N → P (+2). Option A has P, Option B has Q. Thus, Option A is correct without full decoding. Worked: The pattern is each letter shifted forward by 2 positions in the alphabet. S+2=U, O+2=Q, L+2=N, D+2=F, I+2=K, E+2=G, R+2=T. Applying +2 to AGNIVEER: A→C, G→I, N→P, I→K, V→X, E→G, E→G, R→T. Result: CIPKXGGT.

questions.text: A soldier starts from his base camp and walks 10 km North. He turns right and walks 15 km. He turns right again and walks 10 km. Finally, he turns left and walks 5 km. What is the straight-line distance between his final position and the base camp?
questions.solution: Shortcut: Track Net Displacement. North (10 km) and South (10 km) cancel each other out. East movements (15 km + 5 km) add up to 20 km. No net North/South displacement remains. Distance = 20 km. Worked: Let Base be origin (0,0). 1. Walk 10 km North → (0, 10). 2. Turn Right (East), walk 15 km → (15, 10). 3. Turn Right (South), walk 10 km → (15, 0). 4. Turn Left (East), walk 5 km → (20, 0). Final coordinates (20, 0). Distance from (0,0) = √(20² + 0²) = 20 km.

questions.text: Pointing to a woman in a photograph, a man says, 'She is the mother of the only daughter of my son.' How is the woman related to the man?
questions.solution: Shortcut: Work backwards from the speaker. 'My son's only daughter' is the granddaughter. The 'mother of the granddaughter' is the son's wife, i.e., Daughter-in-law. Step-by-step: 1) Speaker's Son. 2) Son's only daughter = Speaker's Granddaughter. 3) Mother of Granddaughter = Son's Wife. 4) Son's Wife = Speaker's Daughter-in-law.

questions.text: Which crop is most characteristically associated with 'Regur Soil' (Black Cotton Soil) found extensively in the Deccan Plateau?
questions.solution: Shortcut: Use the alternative name 'Black Cotton Soil' given in the stem itself. The name 'Cotton' is explicitly embedded in the common nomenclature of the soil. Full Solution: Regur soil, commonly known as Black Cotton Soil, is formed from the weathering of basaltic lava rocks (Deccan Traps). It is rich in lime, iron, magnesia, and alumina but deficient in phosphorus, nitrogen, and organic matter. Its high moisture retention capacity and clayey texture make it ideal for cotton cultivation. It covers most of Maharashtra, parts of Gujarat, Madhya Pradesh, Telangana, Andhra Pradesh, and Tamil Nadu.

questions.text: Who was appointed as the first Governor-General of Bengal under the Regulating Act of 1773?
questions.solution: Shortcut: Chronological elimination. Regulating Act 1773 created the post. Warren Hastings was the serving Governor of Bengal (since 1772) and became the first GG. Cornwallis came later (1786), Wellesley (1798), Bentinck (1828). Full Solution: The Regulating Act of 1773 was the first step by the British Parliament to regulate the affairs of the East India Company in India. It elevated the Governor of Bengal (Warren Hastings) to the position of 'Governor-General of Bengal' and created an Executive Council of four members to assist him. Warren Hastings served from 1773 to 1785. Lord Cornwallis succeeded him in 1786.

questions.text: INS Vikrant (IAC-1), commissioned into the Indian Navy in September 2022, is distinct because it is India's first:

options.label: C
options.text: Indigenously designed and built Aircraft Carrier

questions.solution: Shortcut: Keyword 'Indigenous' + 'Aircraft Carrier'. INS Vikramaditya was purchased from Russia (modified Kiev-class). INS Viraat was ex-HMS Hermes (British). INS Vikrant (IAC-1) is the first built in India (Cochin Shipyard). Full Solution: INS Vikrant (Indigenous Aircraft Carrier-1) is the first aircraft carrier to be designed by the Indian Navy's Directorate of Naval Design and built at Cochin Shipyard Limited for the Indian Navy. It displaces approx 45,000 tonnes. Previous carriers INS Vikrant (R11, 1961), INS Viraat (R22, 1987), and INS Vikramaditya (R33, 2013) were all acquired from the UK or Russia. The ship's motto is 'Jayema Sam Yudhi Spridhah' (I conquer those who fight against me) from Rigveda.

questions.text: Which Fundamental Right was removed from Part III of the Constitution by the 44th Amendment Act, 1978 and subsequently made a legal right under Article 300A?
questions.solution: Shortcut (Option Elimination): The 44th Amendment is famous for reversing the 42nd Amendment's excesses. Options A, B, and D (Equality, Freedom, Remedies) form the 'Golden Triangle' (Articles 14, 19, 21/32) – the basic structure of the Constitution – and can never be removed. Only 'Right to Property' (formerly Art 31) was demoted to a legal right (Art 300A). Step-by-step: 1. Identify the 44th Amendment (1978) context: enacted by Janata Govt to restore constitutional sanity. 2. Recall Art 31 (Right to Property) was a major hurdle for land reforms. 3. The Amendment deleted Art 19(1)(f) and Art 31. 4. Inserted Art 300A: 'No person shall be deprived of his property save by authority of law'. 5. Verify others: Art 14-18 (Equality), Art 19-22 (Freedom), Art 32 (Remedies) remain intact as Fundamental Rights.

questions.text: The Tehri Dam, the highest dam in India and one of the tallest in the world, is constructed on which river?
questions.solution: Shortcut (Association Elimination): Match famous dams to rivers instantly. Bhakra Nangal → Sutlej (Option A). Hirakud → Mahanadi (Option C). Sardar Sarovar → Narmada (Option D). By eliminating the three major dams linked to the other three rivers, the only remaining option for Tehri Dam (Uttarakhand) is Bhagirathi. Step-by-step: 1. Locate Tehri Dam: Tehri Garhwal district, Uttarakhand. 2. Identify the river flowing there: Bhagirathi (headstream of Ganga). 3. Confirm height: 260.5 m (highest in India). 4. Cross-check distractors: Bhakra Dam (Sutlej, Himachal), Hirakud Dam (Mahanadi, Odisha), Sardar Sarovar (Narmada, Gujarat). 5. Conclude Option B is correct.

questions.text: A product marked at ₹800 is sold after two successive discounts of 20% and 10%. What is the selling price?
questions.solution: Shortcut: Effective discount = 20+10−(20×10/100)=28%; Selling price = 800×(100−28)/100 = 800×0.72 = ₹576. Full: After 20% discount price = 800×0.8 = ₹640; after further 10% discount = 640×0.9 = ₹576.

questions.text: A sum of ₹5000 amounts to ₹6200 in 4 years at simple interest. What is the rate of interest per annum?
questions.solution: Shortcut: SI = Amount − Principal = 1200; Rate = (SI×100)/(P×T) = (1200×100)/(5000×4) = 6%. Full: Simple Interest = 6200−5000 = 1200; using formula SI = (P×R×T)/100 → 1200 = (5000×R×4)/100 → R = 6%.

questions.text: In a mixture of 60 litres, the ratio of milk to water is 2:1. How much water must be added to make the ratio 1:2?
questions.solution: Shortcut: Milk remains constant at 40 L. For final ratio 1:2, water should be 2×40 = 80 L. Additional water = 80−20 = 60 L. Full: Initial milk = (2/3)×60 = 40 L, water = 20 L. Let x be added water. Then 40/(20+x) = 1/2 → 80 = 20+x → x = 60 L.

questions.text: The difference between Compound Interest (compounded annually) and Simple Interest on a sum of ₹1600 for 2 years is ₹16. What is the rate of interest per annum?
questions.solution: Shortcut: For 2 years, Difference (CI - SI) = P × (R/100)². Substituting values: 16 = 1600 × (R/100)² ⇒ (R/100)² = 16/1600 = 1/100 ⇒ R/100 = 1/10 ⇒ R = 10%. Full Solution: SI for 2 years = (1600 × R × 2)/100 = 32R. Amount in CI = 1600(1 + R/100)² = 1600(1 + 2R/100 + R²/10000). CI = Amount - P = 32R + 1600×R²/10000 = 32R + 0.16R². Difference = CI - SI = 0.16R² = 16 ⇒ R² = 100 ⇒ R = 10%.

questions.text: A body starts from rest and moves with a uniform acceleration of 5 m/s². What will be its velocity after covering a distance of 20 m?
questions.solution: Shortcut: Use v² = u² + 2as. Since u=0, v = √(2as) = √(2×5×20) = √200 = 10√2 m/s. Option elimination: √2 ≈ 1.414, so value ≈ 14.14 m/s; only option B matches the exact surd form. Step-by-step: Initial velocity u = 0, Acceleration a = 5 m/s², Displacement s = 20 m. Using third equation of motion: v² = 0² + 2(5)(20) = 200. Therefore, v = √200 = 10√2 m/s.

questions.text: What is the number of molecules present in 11 g of Carbon Dioxide (CO₂)? (Avogadro's Number = Nₐ)
questions.solution: Shortcut: Molar mass of CO₂ = 44 g/mol. Given mass (11 g) is exactly 1/4th of molar mass. Moles = 11/44 = 0.25 mol. Molecules = 0.25 Nₐ. Step-by-step: Molar mass of CO₂ = 12 + (2×16) = 44 g/mol. Number of moles = Given Mass / Molar Mass = 11 g / 44 g/mol = 0.25 mol. Number of molecules = Moles × Avogadro's Number = 0.25 × Nₐ = 0.25 Nₐ.

questions.text: The atomic number of an element is 16. Based on its electronic configuration, which of the following correctly identifies its group and period in the Modern Periodic Table?
questions.solution: Shortcut: Atomic number 16 → Electronic configuration = 2, 8, 6. Period = Number of shells = 3. Valence electrons = 6 → p-block element → Group = 10 + Valence electrons = 16. Step-by-step: Electrons fill K-shell (2), L-shell (8), M-shell (6). The presence of 3 shells places it in Period 3. With 6 valence electrons in the outermost shell, it belongs to Group 16 (VIA group) of the p-block.

questions.text: If 'CAT' is coded as '3120' in a certain code language, how will 'DOG' be coded in the same language?
questions.solution: Shortcut: Use alphabetical position values (A=1, B=2... Z=26). CAT -> C(3), A(1), T(20) = 3120. Apply same logic: D(4), O(15), G(7) = 4157. Step-by-step: Write position of each letter in DOG: D=4, O=15, G=7. Concatenate to get 4157.

questions.text: A man walks 10 km North, turns right and walks 5 km, turns right again and walks 10 km, then turns left and walks 10 km. What is the straight-line distance from his starting point?
questions.solution: Shortcut: Track Net Displacement. North-South: +10 (N) -10 (S) = 0. East-West: +5 (E) +10 (E) = 15 km East. Distance = 15 km. Step-by-step: 1. Start (0,0). 2. North 10 -> (0,10). 3. Right (East) 5 -> (5,10). 4. Right (South) 10 -> (5,0). 5. Left (East) 10 -> (15,0). Distance from origin = 15 km.

questions.text: Pointing to a man, a woman says, 'He is the brother of the only daughter of my father.' How is the woman related to the man?
questions.solution: Shortcut: Parse the statement backwards from the known anchor ('my father'). 'Only daughter of my father' = The Speaker (Woman), assuming no sisters. 'Brother of the only daughter' = Brother of the Speaker = The Man. Therefore, the Woman is the Man's Sister. Step-by-step: 1. The speaker is the woman. 2. 'My father' is the woman's father. 3. 'Only daughter of my father' indicates the woman is the sole female child; hence, this phrase refers to the woman herself. 4. 'He is the brother of [the woman]' establishes the man as the woman's brother. 5. Consequently, the woman is the sister of the man.

questions.text: As of January 2024, what is the total number of Constitutional Amendment Acts enacted in India?
questions.solution: Shortcut: The 105th Amendment (2021) restored state powers for OBC lists; the 106th Amendment (Sept 2023) provided 33% women's reservation. No further amendment was enacted by Jan 2024. Step-by-step: The 104th Amendment (2020) extended SC/ST reservation. The 105th came in Aug 2021. The 106th (Nari Shakti Vandan Adhiniyam) received assent in Sept 2023. Hence, the count stands at 106.

questions.text: What is the elevation of Kanchenjunga, the highest mountain peak located entirely within India?
questions.solution: Shortcut: K2 (8,611 m) is in PoK, not fully in India. Kanchenjunga is the 3rd highest globally. Remember the unit digit '6' for Kanchenjunga (8586). Step-by-step: Mount Everest (8,848 m) is in Nepal/China. K2 (8,611 m) lies in Gilgit-Baltistan (PoK). Kanchenjunga (8,586 m) lies on the Sikkim-Nepal border, making it the highest peak entirely within Indian territory. Option A matches the verified elevation.

questions.text: The Battle of Buxar, which established British supremacy in Bengal, was fought in which year?
questions.solution: Shortcut: Use the sequence of major battles: Plassey (1757) -> Panipat (1761) -> Buxar (1764). 1764 is divisible by 4 (leap year), eliminating 1757, 1761, 1756. Step-by-step: Battle of Plassey was 1757. Third Battle of Panipat was 1761. Battle of Buxar was fought on 22 Oct 1764 between British East India Company and the combined forces of Mir Qasim, Shuja-ud-Daulah, and Shah Alam II. The victory led to the Treaty of Allahabad (1765).

questions.text: How many operational and training commands does the Indian Army currently have in total?
questions.solution: Shortcut: Standard Defence GK fact: 6 Operational Commands (Western, Eastern, Northern, Southern, South Western, Central) + 1 Training Command (ARTRAC) = 7. Step-by-step: The Indian Army is organized into 7 commands. Six are operational/field commands headed by GOC-in-C (Lieutenant General). The seventh is the Army Training Command (ARTRAC) at Shimla, responsible for training policies. No new command has been raised recently.

questions.text: As per the Constitution of India, what is the total number of Schedules currently in force?
questions.solution: Shortcut: Use Option Elimination via Amendment tracking. Original Constitution had 8 Schedules. Four major amendments added one Schedule each: 9th (1st Amend), 10th (52nd Amend), 11th (73rd Amend), 12th (74th Amend). 8 + 4 = 12. Eliminate 10, 11, 13. Full Solution: The Indian Constitution originally contained 8 Schedules. The 9th Schedule was added by the 1st Amendment Act, 1951 (Land Reforms). The 10th Schedule was added by the 52nd Amendment Act, 1985 (Anti-Defection Law). The 11th Schedule was added by the 73rd Amendment Act, 1992 (Panchayats). The 12th Schedule was added by the 74th Amendment Act, 1992 (Municipalities). No further Schedules have been added, making the current total 12.

questions.text: A shopkeeper marks an article 40% above its cost price and allows two successive discounts of 20% and 10% respectively. What is his profit or loss percentage?
questions.solution: Shortcut: Equivalent single discount for successive discounts of a% and b% is (a + b - ab/100)%. Here, equivalent discount = 20 + 10 - (20*10/100) = 28%. If CP = 100, MP = 140. SP = 140 * (100-28)/100 = 140 * 0.72 = 100.8. Profit % = 0.8%. Worked: Let CP = ₹100. MP = ₹140. After 20% discount, price = ₹112. After 10% discount, SP = ₹100.80. Profit = ₹0.80 on ₹100 = 0.8%.

questions.text: The difference between Compound Interest and Simple Interest on a certain sum for 2 years at 10% per annum is ₹50. Find the principal sum.
questions.solution: Shortcut: For 2 years, Difference (CI - SI) = P * (R/100)^2. Here, 50 = P * (10/100)^2 = P/100. Therefore, P = 50 * 100 = ₹5,000. Worked: SI for 2 years = P * 10 * 2 / 100 = 0.2P. Amount in CI = P(1 + 10/100)^2 = 1.21P. CI = 0.21P. Difference = 0.21P - 0.2P = 0.01P = 50. Hence, P = 50 / 0.01 = ₹5,000.

questions.text: A ball is thrown vertically upward with an initial velocity of 20 m/s. What is the maximum height reached? (Take g = 10 m/s²)

questions.text: The sides of a triangle are in the ratio 3 : 4 : 5. If the perimeter of the triangle is 48 cm, what is its area (in \(\text{cm}^2\))?
questions.solution: Shortcut: Recognize 3:4:5 as a Pythagorean triplet (right-angled triangle). Let sides be \(3x, 4x, 5x\). Perimeter \(12x = 48 \Rightarrow x = 4\). Sides are 12 cm, 16 cm, 20 cm. Area = \(\frac{1}{2} \times \text{base} \times \text{height} = \frac{1}{2} \times 12 \times 16 = 96\). Step-by-step: Sum of ratio terms = 3+4+5 = 12. Value of one part = 48/12 = 4. Sides = 12, 16, 20. Check right angle: \(12^2 + 16^2 = 144 + 256 = 400 = 20^2\). Area = 0.5 * 12 * 16 = 96 \(\text{cm}^2\).

questions.text: If \( x + \frac{1}{x} = 4 \), what is the value of \( x^3 + \frac{1}{x^3} \)?
questions.solution: Shortcut: Use the identity \( (x + \frac{1}{x})^3 = x^3 + \frac{1}{x^3} + 3(x + \frac{1}{x}) \). Substitute the given value: \( 4^3 = x^3 + \frac{1}{x^3} + 3(4) \Rightarrow 64 = x^3 + \frac{1}{x^3} + 12 \Rightarrow x^3 + \frac{1}{x^3} = 52 \). Step-by-step: Cube both sides of the given equation \( x + \frac{1}{x} = 4 \). The expansion of \( (a+b)^3 \) is \( a^3 + b^3 + 3ab(a+b) \). Here \( a=x, b=\frac{1}{x} \), so \( ab=1 \). Thus \( (x + \frac{1}{x})^3 = x^3 + \frac{1}{x^3} + 3(1)(x + \frac{1}{x}) \). Substitute \( x + \frac{1}{x} = 4 \): \( 64 = x^3 + \frac{1}{x^3} + 12 \). Solving gives \( x^3 + \frac{1}{x^3} = 52 \).

questions.text: In a certain code language, 'MANGO' is written as 'NZMTL'. How is 'APPLE' written in that code?
questions.solution: **Shortcut (Atbash Cipher Rule):** In a reverse alphabet code (Atbash), the sum of the positional values of a plain letter and its coded letter is always 27 (since A=1, Z=26; 1+26=27). To find the code for any letter, subtract its position value from 27. **Step-by-Step Solution:** 1. **Analyze the given example:** M(13) → N(14), A(1) → Z(26), N(14) → M(13), G(7) → T(20), O(15) → L(12). 2. **Identify the pattern:** 13+14=27, 1+26=27, 14+13=27, 7+20=27, 15+12=27. The pattern is Reverse Alphabet (Atbash Cipher). 3. **Apply to 'APPLE':** - A (1) → 27-1 = 26 → **Z** - P (16) → 27-16 = 11 → **K** - P (16) → 27-16 = 11 → **K** - L (12) → 27-12 = 15 → **O** - E (5) → 27-5 = 22 → **V** 4. **Final Code:** **ZKKOV**.

questions.text: A man walks 5 km towards North, turns right and walks 3 km, then turns left and walks 2 km, then turns left and walks 3 km. How far is he from the starting point?
questions.solution: Correct answer: 7 km.

questions.text: Raju walked 30 m towards North, then 20 m towards East, then 30 m towards South. How far and in which direction is he from the starting point?
questions.solution: Correct answer: 20 m East.

questions.text: In a linear seating arrangement, the concepts of leftmost and rightmost are described as absolute references. What does this imply about the ends of the row?

options.label: A
options.text: The leftmost position changes depending on the perspective of the seated persons.

options.label: B
options.text: The leftmost and rightmost positions are fixed and do not change regardless of perspective.

options.label: C
options.text: Only the rightmost position is absolute; the leftmost is relative.

options.label: D
options.text: Neither end is fixed; both are relative to the observer.

questions.solution: Correct answer: The leftmost and rightmost positions are fixed and do not change regardless of perspective..

questions.text: Which category of clue does the statement "A sits third to the left of B" belong to in a linear arrangement puzzle?
questions.solution: Correct answer: Relative clue.

questions.text: What is the primary function of negative clues in linear seating arrangement puzzles?

options.label: A
options.text: They directly assign a person to a specific seat.

options.label: B
options.text: They create a set of possible pairs of slots for two persons.

options.label: C
options.text: They eliminate impossible slots and prune the search space.

options.label: D
options.text: They link two separate arrangement models together.

questions.solution: Correct answer: They eliminate impossible slots and prune the search space..

questions.text: In a circular seating arrangement where all persons face the centre, the direction "clockwise" corresponds to which relative side for each person?
questions.solution: Correct answer: Right.

questions.text: In a sequencing puzzle, the clue "Event C occurs immediately after Event D" translates into which constraints in the directed graph representation?

options.label: B
options.text: An edge D → C and a restriction that no other event can be placed between D and C.

options.label: D
options.text: No edge is added; it only fixes the rank of C.

questions.solution: Correct answer: An edge D → C and a restriction that no other event can be placed between D and C..

questions.text: In a multi‑attribute matrix puzzle, a relational clue states: "The engineer likes cricket." How should this clue be processed during constraint propagation?

options.label: A
options.text: Assign both attributes directly to the engineer without checking other entities

options.label: B
options.text: Intersect the candidate sets of the two linked attributes for that entity; if the intersection becomes a singleton, fix the value and cascade eliminations

options.label: C
options.text: Eliminate all other values for those attributes across all entities immediately

options.label: D
options.text: Treat the clue as a negative clue and remove the engineer‑cricket pair from all entities

questions.solution: Correct answer: Intersect the candidate sets of the two linked attributes for that entity; if the intersection becomes a singleton, fix the value and cascade eliminations.

questions.text: A hybrid puzzle includes an arithmetic constraint: the sum of the floor numbers of three persons equals 12. Each person occupies a distinct floor from 1 to 5. What must the solver ensure when applying this constraint?

options.label: A
options.text: Treat the sum constraint as independent of the distinctness requirement

options.label: B
options.text: Combine the arithmetic constraint with the permutation of distinct values to prune domains

options.label: C
options.text: Ignore distinctness because the sum already limits possibilities

options.label: D
options.text: Assume floors can repeat to satisfy the sum

questions.solution: Correct answer: Combine the arithmetic constraint with the permutation of distinct values to prune domains.

questions.text: In a circular table with 8 equally spaced seats, A sits opposite B. If A is anchored at seat 1, which seat must B occupy?
questions.solution: Correct answer: Seat 5.

questions.text: A multi‑attribute puzzle assigns each person a profession and a floor. The clue "The engineer lives on the third floor" is processed by arc consistency (AC‑3). How are the domains pruned?

options.label: A
options.text: Removes all floors except third from engineer's floor domain and removes engineer from other persons' profession domains

options.label: B
options.text: Removes only the third floor from engineer's floor domain

options.label: C
options.text: Adds engineer to all persons' profession domains

questions.solution: Correct answer: Removes all floors except third from engineer's floor domain and removes engineer from other persons' profession domains.

questions.text: A conditional clue states: "If P sits at position 2 then Q sits at position 4." In an implication graph used for conditional clause chains, how is this clue represented?

options.label: A
options.text: As a directed edge from node (P=2) to node (Q=4)

options.label: B
options.text: As an undirected edge between P and Q

options.label: C
options.text: As a bidirectional edge between (P=2) and (Q=4)

questions.solution: Correct answer: As a directed edge from node (P=2) to node (Q=4).

questions.text: In a linear row of 6 seats, A is to the left of B with at least one person sitting between them. What is the minimum possible number of seats separating A and B?
questions.solution: Correct answer: 2.

questions.text: Floors are numbered 1 to 4. The clue "The engineer's floor number is the square of the teacher's floor number" appears. Which teacher–engineer floor pair is forced by this arithmetic constraint?
questions.solution: Correct answer: Teacher 2, Engineer 4.

questions.text: In a circular seating puzzle, fixing one person breaks rotational symmetry. What additional clue is needed to eliminate the remaining reflection symmetry?

options.label: A
options.text: A clue stating the person faces north

options.label: B
options.text: A clue stating two persons are adjacent

options.label: C
options.text: A clue stating the number of persons is even

options.label: D
options.text: A clue stating the table has a diameter

questions.solution: Correct answer: A clue stating the person faces north.

questions.text: Which propagation method is necessary to enforce a global cardinality constraint like "exactly three doctors" in a seating puzzle?

options.label: B
options.text: Flow-based filtering on a bipartite graph

questions.solution: Correct answer: Flow-based filtering on a bipartite graph.

questions.text: When multiple step-size clues are given on a circular arrangement, which invariant must be checked to avoid inconsistency?

options.label: A
options.text: The sum of all step sizes must equal the number of persons

options.label: B
options.text: The parity (even/odd) of the distance between any two persons must be consistent across all clues

options.label: C
options.text: The step sizes must all be prime numbers

options.label: D
options.text: The clockwise distance must always be less than the anticlockwise distance

questions.solution: Correct answer: The parity (even/odd) of the distance between any two persons must be consistent across all clues.

questions.text: In a puzzle where each profession allows only a subset of colours, what propagation technique removes a profession value when none of its allowed colours remain?

options.label: B
options.text: Support-count propagation from child to parent

questions.solution: Correct answer: Support-count propagation from child to parent.

questions.text: How should the conditional clue "If A sits at position 3 then B is a Doctor" be encoded in a SAT/SMT model?

options.label: A
options.text: As a permanent binary constraint between A's position and B's profession

options.label: C
options.text: As a global cardinality constraint on the number of doctors

options.label: D
options.text: As a parity constraint on the positions

questions.solution: Correct answer: As an implication clause (x_A,3 → y_B,Doctor).

questions.text: In a multi-stage puzzle, three conditionals form a cycle: if A then B, if B then C, and if C then A. What does this cycle force about the truth values of the antecedents?

options.label: A
options.text: All three antecedents must be true

options.label: B
options.text: All three antecedents must be false

options.label: C
options.text: Either all three are true or all three are false

options.label: D
options.text: No definite conclusion can be drawn

questions.solution: Correct answer: Either all three are true or all three are false.

questions.text: A scheduling puzzle includes the clue "A and B cannot overlap". Before branching on the disjunction, which propagation technique can tighten the earliest and latest start bounds of the tasks?

questions.text: A double-row puzzle states "the two rows are mirror images". Which single anchoring constraint is sufficient to break the row-wise reflection symmetry?

options.text: Fix the rightmost person of the second row

options.label: B
options.text: Fix the leftmost person of the first row

options.text: Fix the middle person of both rows

questions.text: In a hybrid seating-resource puzzle, after listing all feasible seat-person pairs from the seating sub-problem, what is the correct next step to verify resource feasibility?

options.label: A
options.text: Assign resources greedily to the highest-ranked persons

options.label: C

questions.text: When a disjunctive clue in a puzzle uses wording that permits both disjuncts to be true, what error occurs if the solver treats it as an exclusive‑or?

questions.text: In the integer linear programming formulation for hybrid seating‑resource puzzles, why does solving the linear relaxation often yield an integral solution for the seating variables?

options.label: A
options.text: Because the seating constraints form a totally unimodular matrix (assignment polytope).

options.label: B
options.text: Because the resource variables are continuous.

options.label: C
options.text: Because the big‑M formulation forces integrality.

options.label: D
options.text: Because the conflict graph is bipartite.

questions.solution: Correct answer: Because the seating constraints form a totally unimodular matrix (assignment polytope)..

questions.text: What is a common mistake when a clue states that a group of persons 'sit together' without specifying their internal order?

options.label: C
options.text: Assuming the group must be split across rows.

options.label: D
options.text: Applying graph coloring to the group.

questions.solution: Correct answer: Treating the group as a rigid block with fixed internal order, over‑constraining the puzzle..
